faq.a: Hyper Tek is a Web3.5 Play-to-Own gaming project in development, with a player-driven marketplace, set in a distant future. It was designed to address major issues in current gaming and digital artwork, giving players greater ownership over their game experience. The ecosystem plans three interconnected games: Hyper Racing, Hyper Quest, and Overlord of the 7 Realms, all sharing one progression system. Rewards for playing are planned to be in-game rewards only.

To understand Web3.5, look at the systemic failures of modern gaming. Traditional Web2 gaming offers polished gameplay, but traps players in closed loops where the items they collect vanish the moment they log off. Early Web3 gaming promised a revolution but delivered a broken experience: volatile tokens, hyperinflation, frustrating crypto wallet barriers, and aggressive pay-to-win mechanics that ruined competitive balance.
Web3.5 is our hybrid architecture designed to bridge this gap. It aims for the frictionless, instant entry of Web2: log in with a standard email and play, while a blockchain backbone records true ownership of your items.

The Core Pillars of the Hyper Tek Ecosystem

Interlinked Three-Game Ecosystem & VR Integration
Web3.5 is designed to unify three distinct game genres, Racing, Quest, and Overlord Realm, into a single ecosystem with shared player progression. Achievements in one world are planned to carry into the others, with VR integration planned for real-time immersive gameplay.

Dynamic Item Interoperability
Items in Hyper Tek are not static images. Every vehicle, item, and modifier is designed with shifting utility. When an item crosses from the racing garage into the Overlord battlefield, its bonuses are planned to shift to match the physics, mechanics, and tactical needs of that environment.

Algorithmic Competitive Balance (Anti-Pay-to-Win)
The ecosystem applies diminishing returns on stacked item bonuses, so raw purchasing power alone should never dominate. While premium items offer distinct strategic utility, the balancing is designed to keep skill as the deciding factor over spending.

Play-to-Own & Digital Collecting
Instead of speculative, inflationary tokens, Hyper Tek focuses on ownership of the items you collect.
Programmatic Trade-In Value: eligible items carry a trade-in allocation held in an on-chain escrow on the Base network, which anyone can verify. The amount returned on a trade-in follows the Tiered Loyalty Return Schedule and is always less than the amount allocated.
Player Marketplace: the marketplace is integrated with player profiles, so players can trade items with each other and upload their own custom items into the ecosystem.

faq.q: What are NFAs, NFCs, and NFTs?
faq.a:
NFAs/NFCs/NFTs are Hyper Tek’s digital artworks. NFAs and NFCs carry in-game bonuses and a Programmatic Trade-In Value.

Non-Fungible Assets (NFAs) are the rarest tier in the Hyper Tek ecosystem. These NFAs are architect-created artworks with the biggest in-game bonuses of any artwork tier. They are released at random when players buy packages and may be awarded as exclusive rewards during major in-game events.

Non-Fungible Collectables (NFCs) also carry in-game bonuses and can be created by both the game architects and by players who follow specific parameters. NFCs open the door for the community to contribute creativity while still gaining gameplay advantages.

Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) are fully player-created artworks. While they do not carry direct in-game bonuses, they can be collected and used to decorate a player’s base or spaceship, and that customisation may contribute to an overall power level bonus.

faq.q: How does the Programmatic Trade-In Value work?
faq.a:
Eligible items carry a trade-in allocation, held in an on-chain escrow that anyone can verify. Part of each first sale, plus 5% of every resale, is added to that item's own allocation.

The owner of an item may trade it in at any time: the item is surrendered and recycled back into the game, and the owner receives an amount set by the Tiered Loyalty Return Schedule, from 80% of the allocation in year one up to 97% after year five. Because part of the allocation is always retained, the amount returned is always less than the amount allocated. It is a product feature, not an investment.

Getting started is simple:

1. Sign up and link your wallet.
2. Explore the marketplace and collect the items you like.

If the games are released, you may be able to complete quests from the Questing Board, tackle daily tasks, join tournaments and events, create digital art, and let out items to other players, all for in-game rewards.

Limited edition NFAs with the largest in-game bonuses are available while supply lasts. They are digital collectibles sold as is, not an investment, and no profit or income is promised.

Three games are currently in development within the Hyper Tek universe and may launch as part of the ecosystem:

Hyper Racing: High-speed circuit racing on alien planets featuring hostile environments. Players may be able to fully upgrade their flying racing vehicles, with racing specialists and pit managers playing crucial roles in reaching the top of the leaderboard.

Hyper Quest: An explorer's dream, offering puzzle-solving missions that take players deep into the known and unknown regions of the Hyper Tek universe, in a kill-or-be-killed environment where every turn could be your last. Rewards are planned to be in-game rewards.

Overlord of the 7 Realms: A tri-level strategy game that focuses on dominion and conquest. Players may command their armies across open terrains while overseeing operations from a strategic orbital position in space, launching attacks, defending territories, and counterattacking across three planes: ground-ground, ground-space, and space-space.

All three games are being designed as interconnected, sharing the same player progression if they launch.

VR and AR support is part of Hyper Tek's design and will become part of the gaming experience as the platform develops. The goal is full cross-platform play, so VR headset, AR, mobile, and traditional players can eventually join the same missions and battles together, from any device.

Once available, we expect the VR/AR layer to open up entirely new ways to experience the Hyper Tek universe.

faq.q: What is a Hyper Tek "Phygital" Asset Certificate?
faq.a:
A Phygital Certificate is a planned bridge between your in-game items and a physical collectible, and may be available if the games are launched. When you buy or mint a premium item on the blockchain, you may be able to use our on-demand printing service to order a high-quality collectible card for that item. For space sectors, you may also be able to order a physical Space Certificate shipped to your home address.

Each card or certificate is planned to carry a gold seal, the item's Base blockchain Token ID, and the item's details from the game database, as a physical keepsake of the item you own.

faq.q: If an item is sold on the marketplace, what happens to the physical certificate?
faq.a: True ownership resides immutably on the Base blockchain, which acts as the ultimate source of truth. Because third-party buyers and sellers can be lazy, players do not need to physically mail cards or paper documents to each other when an asset changes hands. The moment an item transitions to a new owner on the Base network ledger, the previous physical certificate simply becomes a historical collector's item. The new owner listed on the Base blockchain instantly unlocks the programmatic right to log into their Hyper Tek profile and order their own freshly generated, custom physical certificate or deed directly from our fulfillment engine to match their live Base chain asset.

faq.q: Can I order more than one physical certificate for an item I own on the chain?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. You hold absolute sovereignty over your property on the Base blockchain. If your profile is verified as the current on-chain owner of the asset on Base Mainnet, our system allows you to order as many physical cards or deeds for that specific item as you want. There are no limits.

faq.q: Why would a player order multiple physical matching items?
faq.a: Players may choose to order more than one card to swap or trade with friends, guild members, or other collectors at events and gaming meetups. The item's gameplay bonuses and its Programmatic Trade-In Value stay with the on-chain item on the Base blockchain, not with the printed card. Cards are collectibles only, and any trade of a printed card is entirely between the players involved.
